Part of the Quantum & Advanced Compute domain — 54 practices, one delivery standard, every engagement measured against a signed business baseline.

Quantum Machine Learning & Simulation is delivered by an Achala practice team that stays through industrialization. Achala benchmarks every candidate method against a tuned classical solver on your data, and publishes the ledger — result, hardware, cost. Where quantum wins, you invest with confidence; where it does not, you know before the money is spent. Who this is for: strategy and innovation leaders evaluating emerging compute, and CFOs who want evidence before spend.

Verification is the whole game: simulator-to-hardware agreement, error-aware metrics, and comparison against the best classical methods (which are better than most demos admit). Where quantum shows signal, the ledger records it; the classical surrogate fleet keeps shipping value regardless.

blocks.sub: Ansatz screens, classical surrogates and the agreement gate

blocks.x: Quantum-ML programs get seduced when enthusiasm meets hardware access: circuits run before trainability is assessed, barren plateaus eat the budget, and the program has a notebook full of losses and no claim. The discipline screens on paper first, ansatz expressibility and trainability assessed analytically (scaling of gradients, parameter counts, noise sensitivity) before any hardware reservation. Classical surrogates are trained per problem as both baseline and triage: if the surrogate answers the question, the quantum run is unnecessary; if it cannot, the screen says why the quantum attempt might.

The agreement gate keeps claims honest: simulator and hardware results must agree within stated tolerances before any comparison to classical baselines counts, and the versus-classical compare runs on pinned instances with the honest benchmark discipline. The capability ledger records what demonstrably works, which problem classes, what tolerance, what date, and the claim gate means nothing leaves the lab as a claim without a ledger entry.

How do you stop quantum-ML programs from getting seduced?

Trainability screens before training: the expressibility and trainability of the ansatz are established on paper and small simulators first, so the GPU bill follows a screen that says the approach can learn, not hope.
What is "hardware agreement" and why does it matter?
Simulator and hardware results agreeing on the same benchmark: 94–97% on the tasks that run. A quantum result nobody can reproduce on hardware is a rumor, and the claim gate requires the agreement.
Is the classical baseline always in the comparison?
Always: the classical surrogate is the honest opponent, in the chart it wins tasks 1 and 4 outright. The claim gate requires beating the classical baseline on the problem that matters, not on a toy.
Can you work with our chemistry lab systems?

Yes, the integration surface names simulators, hardware access and lab systems. Candidate molecules and validation data enter through typed seams, and results return in the formats the lab already trusts.

The dual-track pipeline, the console with agreement as the headline, the claim gate and the research governance overlay, claims that survive are reproducible, and the ones that do not were killed cheaply.
